study type: secondary analysis of survey and medical chart data
cohort: 380 high-risk, low-income, predominantly Black and Latina women in New York City who were Medicaid-insured and enrolled in an intervention to improve timely postpartum visits from 2015 to 2016
finding: Black race, US-born, English speaking, cesarean delivery, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and positive depression or anxiety screen were associated with increased odds of postpartum hospital use, while breastfeeding at three weeks postpartum was associated with decreased odds of postpartum hospitalization.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with increased odds of postpartum hospital use.
